classification.habit: Small deciduous to semi-deciduous shrub or small tree, often branched from the base
classification.habitat: Cultivated and naturalized in warm, relatively dry regions; tolerates seasonal drought
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated in India; distribution varies with cultivar and region

identification.description: Recognized by its branched habit, opposite or clustered narrow leaves, showy reddish flowers and characteristic leathery fruit with a persistent calyx.
identification.whole_plant: Much-branched shrub or small tree with grey-brown to reddish-brown bark and dense foliage.
identification.root: Woody root system; bark identity should be confirmed on authenticated material.
identification.stem: Young branches are slender and may bear short spine-like branch tips; older stems become woody with grey-brown bark.
identification.leaf: Simple, entire, glossy, narrow-oblong to lanceolate leaves, usually opposite or in short clusters.
identification.flower: Solitary or clustered, conspicuous red to orange-red flowers with a persistent calyx.
identification.fruit: Globose pomegranate fruit with tough leathery rind, persistent crown-like calyx and numerous arillate seeds internally separated by membranes.
identification.seed: Numerous angular seeds surrounded by juicy translucent arils; seed characters vary with cultivar.
identification.bark: Grey-brown outer bark on mature stems; bark microscopy should be performed on authenticated material.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Punica granatum is extensively studied for its fruit and polyphenol-rich fractions. This dossier does not convert experimental evidence into a clinical efficacy claim.

modern_information.safety_notes: Use correctly identified plant material. Evidence and safety can differ by fruit, peel, bark, root and extract; do not interchange plant parts without source-specific support.
